outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Recurrent Architectures and the Original LSTM
outline.description: This chapter provides the foundational knowledge necessary to understand xLSTM, starting with the basics of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and a deep dive into the original LSTM architecture.
subtopics: The Vanishing Gradient Problem in RNNs
The Constant Error Carousel (CEC) concept
The anatomy of a classic LSTM cell: Cell state and Hidden state
The role of Gating: Input, Forget, and Output gates
Activation functions in LSTMs: Sigmoid and Tanh
Historical success stories of LSTMs in sequence modeling

outline.chapter_title: Identifying the Bottlenecks: Why LSTMs Were Outpaced
outline.description: Before introducing xLSTM, this chapter explores the three fundamental limitations that allowed Transformer and State Space Model (SSM) architectures to dominate the field.
subtopics: The Storage Revision Problem: Analysis of the Nearest Neighbor Search task
The Capacity Bottleneck: Why scalar memory struggles with Rare Token Prediction
The Sequential Processing Constraint: Memory mixing and the lack of parallelizability
Comparing LSTM memory to Transformer self-attention
The motivation for xLSTM: Scaling LSTMs to billions of parameters

outline.chapter_title: sLSTM: Exponential Gating and Scalar Memory Evolution
outline.description: This chapter explains the first major component of xLSTM: the sLSTM, focusing on how exponential gating allows the model to revise storage decisions and maintain stability.
subtopics: From Sigmoid to Exponential Gating: Enabling storage revision
The Normalizer State ($n_t$): Ensuring mathematical consistency
Numerical Stability: The Stabilizer State ($m_t$) and overflow prevention
The sLSTM forward pass: Detailed step-by-step derivation
Memory Mixing in sLSTM: Recurrent connections and the introduction of heads

outline.description: This chapter introduces the mLSTM, which solves the capacity problem by upgrading scalar memory to matrix memory and enabling parallel computation.
subtopics: The concept of Matrix Memory: Moving beyond scalars
The Covariance Update Rule: Storing key-value pairs
Retrieval mechanism: Query, Key, and Value (QKV) framework
Normalizing retrieval in mLSTM: Using the normalizer state dot-product
Breaking the sequential chain: How mLSTM achieves full parallelizability
Comparison between mLSTM and Bidirectional Associative Memories (BAMs)

outline.description: This chapter details how sLSTM and mLSTM are integrated into a larger, scalable deep learning architecture using modern residual blocks.
subtopics: xLSTM Blocks: Combining sLSTM and mLSTM
Cover's Theorem and the importance of high-dimensional embedding
Residual Block Backbones: Pre up-projection vs. Post up-projection
Choosing the backbone: Why mLSTM uses pre up-projection and sLSTM uses post up-projection
Residually stacking blocks: Depth, LayerNorm, and overall network topology

outline.description: This chapter examines the experimental evidence that proves xLSTM's superiority in specific tasks, focusing on state tracking and memory recall.
subtopics: Solving State Tracking: Performance on formal languages and regular grammars
Testing Memory Capacity: The Multi-Query Associative Recall task
Handling Long Sequences: Evaluation on the Long Range Arena (LRA)
The synergy between sLSTM and mLSTM in hybrid architectures (xLSTM[a:b])

outline.chapter_title: xLSTM as a Large Language Model: Scaling and Performance
outline.description: The final chapter explores the results of scaling xLSTM to billions of parameters and compares it against industry-standard Transformers and SSMs.
subtopics: Large-scale training on the SlimPajama dataset
Perplexity and Validation: Comparing xLSTM, Llama, Mamba, and RWKV
Sequence Length Extrapolation: Maintaining performance across longer contexts
Downstream Task Performance: Common sense reasoning and PALOMA benchmarks
Scaling Laws: Predicting the performance of larger xLSTM models
Computational Efficiency: Inference throughput, memory complexity, and generation time
